title: Harnessing Adaptability
coreMove: Diagnose what a training demand is actually teaching before trusting strain as improvement.
sourcePressure: The chapter explains that bodies and minds adapt under repeated demand, so apparent limits can move, but the adaptation follows the training pattern whether useful or harmful. Frozen sidecar for chapter 2 contains no traceable named figure, study, place, date, or artifact beyond the authors and chapter mechanism; sourceAnchors stays empty rather than inventing one.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says discomfort proves growth and limits are just mindset errors.

examples: runner adding mileage with bad form from old modern package

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: ceramics studio centering clay on a wheel
exampleSpecs.audience: a beginner who confuses sore wrists with progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: bad hand pressure is becoming the normal feel before she notices it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire stops after three collapsed bowls, checks the wobble line in the clay wall, lowers the wheel speed, and trains one centered pull instead of forcing more ruined bowls
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wet clay slapping unevenly against the heel of a hand

exampleSpecs.domain: pharmacy technician dosage-label accuracy under timed drills
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainee who thinks speed drills are helping because they feel intense
exampleSpecs.stakes: rushing labels could make the wrong dose feel fluent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 2:42 p.m., David compares the error log, sees that every timed drill trains abbreviation slips, and switches to a slower demand: five perfect labels before speed returns
exampleSpecs.firstImage: orange prescription labels curling from a printer tray

exampleSpecs.domain: choir breath-control work for a long phrase
exampleSpecs.audience: a singer who keeps singing louder when the phrase thins out
exampleSpecs.stakes: the choir section is adapting to neck tension instead of supported breath
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie asks the section to sing the phrase at half volume with hands on ribs, then records whether the last note stays steady before adding volume back
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sheet music corners lifting in the draft from an old rehearsal-room fan

exampleSpecs.domain: warehouse hand-scan accuracy during holiday order pressure
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations lead whose team is adapting to speed metrics
exampleSpecs.stakes: the scanner rhythm rewards fast wrong picks that customers return later
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Henrik maps returns to scan pace, removes the speed leaderboard for one aisle, and trains a pause at the SKU suffix before the next shift
exampleSpecs.firstImage: returned shipping labels stacked beside a handheld scanner cradle

exampleSpecs.audience: a bilingual professional whose fast shadowing is flattening meaning
exampleSpecs.stakes: speed without accuracy could train omissions under pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Isabel replay one minute of testimony, mark every omitted qualifier, and lower the playback speed until accuracy adapts before speed returns
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a transcript margin filled with small circles around qualifiers

exampleSpecs.domain: youth basketball free-throw mechanics after a growth spurt
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach seeing a taller player adapt around new limbs
exampleSpecs.stakes: the player is making awkward compensation feel permanent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Yusuf predicts misses from elbow flare on video, moves the tape mark under the shooting foot, and requires recovery between sets so the new alignment can settle
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a strip of red tape under one shoe on the foul line

skillTargets: separate useful strain from blind strain
explain why recovery is part of adaptation
choose a clean demand that changes capacity without training the wrong habit

tryThisNowSpec: Look at one hard routine you already do. Write the demand it is placing on you, the habit it may be strengthening, and one change that would make the signal cleaner before the next rep.
